title: Śrī Śikṣāṣṭakam
author: by Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu in Sanskrit
subtitle: Verse Two

translation: “O my Lord, Your Holy Name bestows auspiciousness upon all. And You have unlimited Names such as Kṛṣṇa and Govinda by which You reveal Yourself. In Your many Holy Names You have kindly invested all Your transcendental potency. And in chanting these Names, there are no strict rules concerning time or place. Out of Your causless mercy, You have descended in the form of divine sound, but my great misfortune is that I have no love for Your Holy Name.”
*Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s corresponding Bengali composition:*
O Lord! You are an ocean of mercy, and so you have brought the teachings of the glories of your unlimited Holy Names to deliver all souls.
You have conferred all Your power upon Your Name. And there are no rules governing the appropriate time or place for chanting the Holy Name.
The Holy Name is a chintāmaṇi gem, a divine touchstone, and is non-different from You. Out of Your kindness for all souls, You have distributed Your Holy Name throughout the universe.
This is Your mercy, O Lord. You are supremely kind. But, O Lord, I am most wicked and unfortunate.
I have never known any attraction for the Holy Names. And so, the heart of Bhakti Vinod is filled with sadness.
